articles.title: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL’s ‘Next Great’ Cornerback
articles.summary: Washington Commanders will get NFL's "Next Great" cornerback back in Week 6 against 49ers. The post Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL’s ‘Next Great’ Corne...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time.

Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions.

Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football.

The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal.

"SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week."

Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders

By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated.

"Trey Amos has no hobbies," Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. "No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back."

Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil .

Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field.

"My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account.

Amos started training camp on the PUP list but returned to practice a few weeks later … and automatically got hurt again.

"Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day," The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return."

Trey Amos Called NFL's 'Next Great Cornerback'

Pro Football Focus NFL reporter Bradley Locker named Amos to his 2026 NFL All-Breakout Team — his list of the NFL's "Next Great" players at every position.

"Last year's second-round selection didn't enjoy the kind of rookie showcase he desired, concluding with a 55.8 overall PFF grade with a 58.8 PFF coverage mark," Locker wrote in May. "While Amos was certainly victimized at times, he reflected his talent by earning at least a 68.5 coverage grade in five of his 10 contests, and his 51.43% lockdown rate was 26 th among all cornerbacks. Further, Amos broke up an eye-catching 17.6% of his targets. Washington's defense should be considerably better at all three levels in 2026 after the team's offseason overhaul. With new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones specializing in the secondary, that marks another boost for Amos."

articles.title: Clippers reportedly re- sign 6-foot-5, high-upside versatile wing just 48 hours after releasing him
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers made an interesting move on Friday. The organization brought back a familiar face after just waiving him.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers are among the many teams around the league finalizing their rosters by waiving players. The Clippers have had quite the offseason, to say the least, and are looking to put all the noise behind them and focus on having a successful season.

LA has been making roster moves throughout the week. One of those moves was waiving former second-round pick Cam Christie.

"The Los Angeles Clippers are waiving Cam Christie, league sources told hoopshype. Christie had a $2.30 million salary guarantee date that was approaching. Christie, who recently turned 21, was the 46th pick of the 2024 NBA Draft and spent the past two seasons with the Clippers," HoopsHype's Michael Scotto wrote.

Christie didn't have much of an impact on the Clippers, as he rarely had the opportunity to play meaningful minutes.

"Christie was the 46th pick in the 2024 NBA Draft and a guy the Clippers were excited to select with their pick. But in the two seasons he's been with the franchise, he's been unable to make strides large enough to warrant an increase in minutes. Aside from that, there weren't many minutes available to him to play, learn through his mistakes, and develop as the Clippers attempted to compete for a deep playoff run," ClutchPoints' Tomar Azarly wrote.

However, on Friday, LA decided to bring Christie back on a two-way deal, just 48 hours after he cleared waivers.

"The Los Angeles Clippers and Cam Christie have agreed to a two-way deal, agent Kevin Bradbury of LIFT Sports Management told hoopshype. Christie, who recently turned 21, was the 46th pick of the 2024 NBA Draft and spent the past two seasons with the Clippers," Scotto posted.

At first glance, the Clippers' decision to bring Christie back so quickly might seem surprising, but the move makes sense. Christie had been on the standard rookie contract he signed after being drafted, and with the opportunity to sign a two-way deal available after he cleared waivers, both sides agreed to move forward.

This allows LA to continue developing Christie while giving him another opportunity to remain with the organization. Spending much-needed time in the G League could help him improve his game and work toward earning a larger role with the Clippers.

articles.title: Every NFL Team's Biggest Surprise of 2026 Entering Week 6
articles.summary: The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season are in the books. Anyone saying things have gone as expected probably isn't being honest.
articles.body:
The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season are in the books. Anyone saying things have gone as expected probably isn't being honest.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans got their first wins of the season in Week 5, but three other teams remain winless heading into the weekend. The Cleveland Browns, New York Giants, and Las Vegas Raiders have three wins apiece, while only the San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, and Minnesota Vikings remain undefeated.

The early season has been filled with unexpected results. Every team has seen individual surprises, too. Let's examine each squad's biggest surprise based on factors like offseason expectations, on-field production, projected upside, and relevant recent buzz.

To be clear, we'll focus on positive surprises here. There's still a lot of the season left, so there's plenty of time to look at what went wrong.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

The offseason addition of linebacker Jack Gibbens may have flown under the radar, even for Arizona Cardinals fans. The 2022 undrafted free agent out of Missouri made eight starts for the New England Patriots in 2025 but was not viewed as a marquee signing.

Gibbens joined Arizona on a modest two-year, $7.5 million contract.

However, the 27-year-old has quickly made himself an integral part of Nick Rallis' defense. He has started four of five games and played 91 percent of the defensive snaps—along with 27 percent of special-teams snaps. Gibbens has already recorded 35 tackles, a half-sack, one tackle for loss, and three quarterback pressures.

Cardinals fans should get used to hearing Gibbens' name on game days.

The Atlanta Falcons have looked like an entirely different team since getting Michael Penix Jr. back into the lineup at quarterback. His ability to stretch the field has really opened up the league's second-ranked rushing attack.

Naturally, Bijan Robinson has been a huge part of Atlanta's offense. He's making an early run at Offensive Player of the Year with 732 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns. However, backup Brian Robinson Jr. is performing surprisingly well in a complementary role.

Signed to a one-year, $1.5 million deal , Robinson may have been viewed as pure depth behind Bijan coming into the season. However, he's given the Falcons a legitimate two-pronged backfield, with a punishing running style that perfectly complements Bijan in Atlanta's wide-zone-based offense.

Through five weeks, Brian Robinson has tallied 210 rushing yards, 21 receiving yards, and four touchdowns.

Unlike many players on this list, Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry hasn't surprised because he wasn't an established star. However, he continues to defy what is expected of older running backs in the NFL.

Despite turning 32 in January—which is older for a pro ball-carrier—Henry insisted that retirement isn't even under consideration.

"My mindset is how can I get better, so we can be the best team we can be," Henry said in July, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley .

Henry continues to be one of the league's biggest mismatches at running back. He's tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for the league lead in rushing touchdowns by running backs with seven—Josh Allen leads all players with eight—and has averaged 95.2 rushing yards and 107.6 scrimmage yards per game.

Only four other backs have more rushing yards than Henry this season.

The Buffalo Bills' 30th-ranked defense has been an issue in 2026. However, Buffalo is sitting at 4-1 because its offense has been one of the most productive in the league.

Guard Alec Anderson has been a huge part of Buffalo's offensive success, which has likely surprised most fans.

A 2022 undrafted free agent out of UCLA, Anderson has long been a valuable depth piece for the Bills. However, he beat out free-agent addition Austin Corbett for the left-guard role in camp and hasn't looked back.

Austin has started every game and played 100 percent of the offensive snaps through five weeks. He has now also played more offensive snaps in 2026 than his previous career-high in a season.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young struggled to establish himself as a reliable starter early in his career. However, the 2023 first overall pick did settle in last season, going 8-8 and leading the Panthers to an NFC South title.

While some may have expected Young to make another jump in Year 4, his explosion through the early season has been stunning. The 25-year-old has come out slinging the ball and playing like a viable MVP candidate.

While the Panthers are just 2-2, Young has looked like one of the biggest playmakers in the game. He has already thrown for 1,268 yards—which led the NFL through four full weeks—with nine touchdowns, two interceptions, and a 100.0 QB rating.

Young's previous career-high passer rating was 87.8 last year.

It probably shouldn't be a total shock that Kalif Raymond is off to one of the best starts of his NFL career with the Chicago Bears. The former Detroit Lions role player has long been one of the NFL's most underrated pass-catchers . He's obviously quite familiar with Ben Johnson's offense.

Still, it's surprising to see Raymond emerge as such a critical piece of Chicago's offense at this stage of his career.

The 32-year-old ranks second on the team in receptions (24) and third in receiving yards (266) through five games, ahead of more notable players like Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze. He's currently on pace for 82 catches, 904 yards, and four touchdowns.

Raymond's best statistical season to date was his 47-catch, 616-yard campaign in 2022.

When discussing Cincinnati Bengals receivers, the conversation is typically centered around headliners Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. However, the Bengals appear to have some strong receiver depth this season, due in large part to the surprising emergence of Dohnte Meyers.

Meyers hasn't put up eye-popping numbers this season, though his seven catches and 82 yards in Week 4 did stand out. His path to playing time in Cincinnati is the surprising part.

Undrafted out of Delta State in 2023, Meyers eventually made his way to the Saskatchewan Roughriders in the CFL, where he played for two seasons. He signed a futures contract with the Bengals in January, shined in the preseason, and has emerged as an important role player.

Meyers has caught 13 passes, returned seven punts, and fielded 16 kickoffs through the first five games of his NFL career.

The Cleveland Browns fell back to earth in Week 5, but their 3-2 record to start the season is still surprising. So has the respectable play of quarterback Deshaun Watson, whose Browns tenure before 2026 was largely a disaster.

Rookie receiver Denzel Boston has played a huge role in the success of both Watson and Cleveland. The second-round pick out of Washington has been unexpectedly productive right out of the gate.

Boston was the seventh receiver drafted in April and wasn't even the first receiver drafted by the Browns—Cleveland used one of its two first-round selections on Texas A&M's K.C. Concepcion . Yet, he currently leads all rookies with 330 receiving yards and three touchdowns. He also leads the NFL with an average of 20.6 yards per catch.

According to ESPN's Rich Cimini , Boston became the new favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year following Week 5.

The Dallas Cowboys added several notable players to their defense this offseason, including trade acquisition Rashan Gary and first-round picks Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence .

By comparison, third-round rookie Jaishawn Barham was probably viewed as more of an afterthought.

However, the Michigan product has quickly become an important piece of Christian Parker's defense. He got a chance at a bigger role when DeMarvion Overshown went down with a hamstring injury. He's run with the opportunity. Through five games, Barham has made four starts and recorded 28 tackles, four tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. He's even worn the green dot for Parker.

"I'm very, very pleased with Jaishawn and his development," Parker said, per team reporter Tommy Yarrish .

Barham was graded 31st overall among all linebackers by Pro Football Focus after Week 5.

The Denver Broncos' defense seemed to regress early in the season. However, it has started to rebound during the team's 4-2 start.

2025 fourth-round pick Quandarrius "Que" Robinson has been a big part of the unit's return to form. He has also seen a surprising jump in production in his second season.

The Alabama product was largely buried on the depth chart as a rookie and saw limited action in six games last season.

Robinson played just 34 percent of the defensive snaps last season and finished with 12 tackles and a half-sack. He has played 47 percent of the snaps through five games this season and has already recorded 23 tackles, three tackles for loss, four quarterback hits, and two sacks.

The Detroit Lions have spent several years searching for a dependable pass-rushing complement to star Aidan Hutchinson. They threw a couple of darts at the role this offseason by signing D.J. Wonnum to a one-year, $3 million deal and using a second-round pick on Michigan's Derrick Moore .

While Moore has played just 19 percent of defensive snaps through the first month of 2026, Wonnum has emerged as a significant piece of Kelvin Sheppard's defense.

The 28-year-old has started two of Detroit's five games and has played 56 percent of the defensive snaps. He has already recorded an impressive 10 tackles, a team-high five sacks, eight quarterback pressures, four tackles for loss, and one batted pass.

Despite battling a back injury, Wonnum has still boosted the pass rush and is on pace to surpass his career-high of 8 sacks in a season sooner rather than later.

The fact that 2025 first-round pick Matthew Golden has stepped into a more prominent role this season wasn't a surprise. Green Bay drafted him to be a long-term go-to target. They created more opportunities for him during the offseason.

The Packers let Romeo Doubs depart in free agency and traded Dontayvion Wicks, effectively making Golden the No. 2 perimeter target opposite Christian Watson.

Still, Golden's production through the first month of the season has been a pleasant surprise, given his ineffectiveness as a rookie last season.

Golden was limited by shoulder and wrist injuries last season. However, his 29 catches and 361 yards in 14 games were still viewed as a disappointment. He's been dramatically better this year, though, and has already compiled 24 catches for 397 yards and two touchdowns.

The Houston Texans have struggled defensively through the first five weeks of the 2026 season, which is a massive negative surprise. However, linebacker Jake Hansen has been a surprise for more positive reasons.

The 2022 undrafted free agent out of Illinois has been with the Texans since entering the NFL. However, he spent the vast majority of his career before this season as a core special-teamer.

Hanson saw his most extensive defensive action as a rookie, when he played 27 percent of the snaps.

Hansen still contributes on special teams, but he's been far more actively involved on defense this season. The 28-year-old has started four of five games and played 80 percent of the snaps. He has recorded 32 tackles, three tackles for loss, one interception, and one sack while allowing a career-best opposing passer rating of 59.9 in coverage.

Wide receivers who are considered a "draft bust" rarely make it to their 11th NFL season. However, that is exactly what Laquon Treadwell has done. He's been surprisingly impactful for the Indianapolis Colts in his latest campaign.

Originally drafted 23rd overall by the Minnesota Vikings in 2016, Treadwell never emerged as an offensive force in Minnesota and lasted just four years with the franchise. The Colts represent the sixth team he's played for.

Treadwell has largely been a special-teamer since arriving in Indy in 2024. Through his first two seasons with the Colts, Treadwell played a total of 43 offensive snaps.

Treadwell is contributing on special teams, but he's been heavily involved in the offense, too, due in part to injuries and the offseason trade of Michael Pittman Jr. He has played 72 percent of the offensive snaps and has caught 11 of 19 targets for 157 yards—his highest totals with any team since 2021.

Fans can expect to hear trade chatter involving third-year receiver Brian Thomas Jr. between now and the November 10 trade deadline for a couple of reasons. For one, Parker Washington has firmly established himself as Jacksonville's new No. 1 target.

Secondly, sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron has been surprisingly involved in the offensive game plan.

The Baylor product has caught a modest eight passes for 117 yards and two touchdowns. However, he has played 31 percent of the offensive snaps, posted a 137.8 passer rating when targeted, and has quickly earned quarterback Trevor Lawrence's trust.

"Every route, you know he's running it to win," Lawrence told reporters about Cameron. "Every time he has a chance to block someone, he's trying to put them in the ground."

Cameron has more receiving yards and touchdowns than Thomas over the first five weeks.

Kansas City Chiefs undrafted free agent Kahlil Benson has been one of the biggest surprises on any NFL roster through the first month of the season. The Colorado product landed in Kansas City as a tryout player in rookie camp. He has since become one of Kansas City's most important players.

Not only did Benson make the active roster, but he also earned the starting job at left tackle to open the season after 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons was sidelined with a back injury.

Benson has started all four games and has played 100 percent of the offensive snaps thus far. Through four games, he has been flagged twice but has not allowed a sack, according to Pro Football Focus .

The NFL named Benson as its Offensive Rookie of the Month for September.

The Raiders are arguably the biggest surprise in the NFL last season. A franchise that won three games in 2025 has already matched last year's win total and came excruciatingly close to knocking off the Chiefs two weeks ago.

This past week, Las Vegas got its first look at rookie quarterback and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza . However, Mendoza saw the field because of the score, not because starter Kirk Cousins was playing poorly.

Cousins' play has been nearly as stunning as the Raiders' accelerated turnaround. The 38-year-old has been a Pro Bowler, but he signed a one-year, $11.3 million deal in the offseason and was largely viewed as a pure placeholder at quarterback.

At some point, Las Vegas will turn the keys over to Mendoza on a full-time basis. With the way Cousins is playing, it just might not happen in 2026.

Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and ranks second in the NFL (tied) with 12 touchdown passes. He's completing 65.1 percent of his passes. His passer rating of 100.7 is his highest since 2023—a season in which Cousins was on a roll before suffering a season-ending Achilles tear.

The Los Angeles Chargers haven't had much to feel good about during their 0-5 start, especially offensively. However, they have to be pleased with the rapid development and performance of rookie offensive tackle Travis Burke .

The fourth-round pick out of Memphis was expected to be a purely developmental prospect behind starting tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt. However, he has seen offensive snaps in each of the past two weeks and made his first career start in Week 5.

Slater landed on injured reserve with an ankle sprain, while Alt is dealing with a neck injury.

Burke played 69 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 4, then 100 percent in Week 5. He has handled himself well thus far. Pro Football Focus graded him 36th overall among all qualifying tackles after five weeks.

As a rookie last season, Konata Mumpfield didn't see much action in the Los Angeles Rams' offense. He played just 33 percent of the snaps and finished with 10 catches for 92 yards and a touchdown.

While Mumpfield's biggest 2026 opportunities came while Puka Nacua was sidelined by hip and groin injuries, the former seventh-round pick out of Pittsburgh was unexpectedly effective in a larger role.

Mumpfield caught four passes for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Week 3 win over the Broncos. He's up to six catches for 112 yards on the season. He has played 40 percent of the offensive snaps through five games.

While Mumpfield figures to be only a part-time player when Nacua and Davante Adams are both healthy, his early-season production should give Los Angeles a lot of confidence in its receiver depth moving forward.

To be fair, a big bulk of Ollie Gordon II's 2026 production came in the Week 4 loss to the Vikings. However, the 2025 sixth-round pick's ability to keep the Miami Dolphins' ground game afloat after De'Von Achane's injury has been unexpectedly impressive.

Achane was arguably the only proven playmaker the Dolphins' offense retained through the offseason. When he suffered a season-ending ACL tear in Week 3, it felt like Miami's rushing offense could be hamstrung for the rest of the season. However, Gordon has looked like a viable lead back over the past three weeks.

After recording just 199 rushing yards and three touchdowns as a rookie, Gordon has already surpassed those numbers in 2026. He had 100 yards and a score against Minnesota. He's up to 236 yards and three touchdowns for the season.

For the season, Gordon has averaged a strong 5.0 yards per carry.

Minnesota Vikings: DL Levi Drake Rodriguez

The Vikings are one of only three undefeated teams. They've been winning largely with defense to this point. They've gotten rather average play from quarterbacks Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray so far and lost star receiver Justin Jefferson for a couple of games to an ankle injury suffered in Week 3.

However, Minnesota's defense has been good enough to secure a 5-0 record. Defensive lineman Levi Drake Rodriguez has been a surprisingly big part of the unit's success.

A 2024 seventh-round pick out of Texas A&M–Commerce, Rodriguez was a high-end contributor last season but has established himself as a full-time starter this season. He has helped Minnesota maintain a disruptive defensive front even after the team parted ways with Javon Hargrave, Jonathan Allen, and Jonathan Greenard during the offseason.

Rodriguez has started all five games, played 58 percent of the defensive snaps, and has recorded nine tackles, a sack, and five quarterback pressures.

Things haven't exactly gone according to plan during the Patriots' 3-2 start. Quarterback Drake Maye was one of the biggest disappointments of the early campaign, though he and New England have started to rebound.

Linebacker Elijah Ponder, however, has been a pleasant surprise since the start.

The 2025 undrafted free agent out of California Polytechnic made his way to New England after shining at the East-West Shrine Bowl. He appeared in 15 games as a rookie but played just 24 percent of the defensive snaps. This year, Ponder has grown into a much more prominent role.

Ponder has started four of the Patriots' first five games and has played 73 percent of the defensive snaps. He has already recorded 19 tackles, 4.5 sacks, 11 QB pressures, six tackles for loss, two fumble recoveries, and a defensive touchdown.

New England has a history of uncovering overlooked talent. It seems it has another gem in Ponder.

The New Orleans Saints acquired wide receiver Devaughn Vele in a 2025 trade with Denver. The 2024 seventh-round pick out of Utah was purely a complementary receiver in his first season with New Orleans, but he's been thrust into a surprisingly large role this season.

In 2025, Vele played 51 percent of the offensive snaps and recorded 25 catches for 293 yards and two touchdowns in 13 games. His season was cut short by a shoulder injury.

This season, Vele is healthy and has filled the No. 2 receiver role opposite Chris Olave. Rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson was supposed to fill that role but has been sidelined by a hamstring injury. In Tyson's absence, Vele has shown that he's more than capable.

The 28-year-old has played 92 percent of the offensive snaps and has already caught 25 passes for 252 yards and two scores. He has provided a passer rating of 104.8 when targeted. He should allow New Orleans to ease Tyson into a prominent role once the rookie is ready to return.

Longtime Baltimore head coach John Harbaugh took the New York Giants' job early in the offseason. Shortly after free agency opened, former Ravens tight end Isaiah Likely joined him in New York.

The 26-year-old pass-catcher has become an unexpected star in New York.

It hasn't been entirely surprising to see Likely perform well for the Giants. He regularly flashed his ability as Baltimore's No. 2 tight end behind Mark Andrews. However, few expected Likely to become one of the league's most dangerous tight ends as the Giants' starter.

Likely has played a career-high 70 percent of the offensive snaps this season. He has already caught 33 passes for 284 yards and four touchdowns. After five full weeks, he ranks fourth in receiving yards among tight ends, behind only Sam LaPorta, Brock Bowers, and Trey McBride.

The New York Jets have been steadily searching for a reliable No. 2 receiver opposite Garrett Wilson. While Isaiah Williams might not be a true second option, he has emerged as a surprisingly effective complementary receiver.

A 2024 undrafted free agent out of Illinois, Williams spent 2024 with the Lions and Bengals before joining the Jets' practice squad last season. He appeared in 15 games and scored two punt-return touchdowns, though his impact was largely limited to special teams.

Williams continues to serve as a dangerous returner, but he's also carved out a more prominent offensive role this season. He has played 75 percent of the offensive snaps through the first five weeks and ranks second among Jets wideouts, behind Wilson, with 151 yards and a touchdown on 11 receptions.

Philadelphia Eagles: WR Dontayvion Wicks

The Philadelphia Eagles put multiple resources into their receiving corps before trading No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown to the Patriots this past offseason. They signed Marquise Brown, traded for Dontayvion Wicks, and used a first-round pick on USC's Makai Lemon .

For most fans, Wicks was probably the afterthought of the group. A sporadic role player for the Packers, Wicks was acquired for a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick. He then signed a modest one-year, $12.5 million extension.

While Wicks was expected to be a complementary receiver in Sean Mannion's offense, he quickly established himself as the No. 2 option opposite DeVonta Smith.

Wicks has started all five games and has filled the No. 1 receiver role in the two games Smith has missed with a hamstring injury. The 25-year-old now leads the Eagles with 260 yards and a touchdown on 17 receptions.

Pittsburgh Steelers: S Robert Spears-Jennings

Late-round rookies often struggle to make the active rosters of playoff-caliber teams. However, former Oklahoma defensive back Robert Spears-Jennings , who was selected in the seventh round (224th overall), has done more than simply stick with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Spears-Jennings has filled a valuable rotational role over the first five weeks while also serving as a core special-teams player. He has played 25 percent of defensive snaps and 73 percent of special-teams snaps, while earning a reputation as a very physical defender.

"He'll come down, lay wood every single time," linebacker Patrick Queen told reporters about Spears-Jennings (beginning around the 3:10 mark). "So, definitely love him back there."

Spears-Jennings has played over 50 percent of the defensive snaps in each of the last two games and has tallied 16 tackles and an interception on the season.

Under normal circumstances, it wouldn't be a surprise to see George Kittle racing up and down the field, delivering crushing blocks and carving up opposing secondaries. However, it's still a bit astonishing to see Kittle back in All-Pro form so soon after suffering a torn Achilles.

The San Francisco 49ers' standout tight end suffered the injury during San Francisco's playoff victory over the Eagles on January 11. Not only was he back on the field for the season opener less than 10 months after the injury, but he's already looking like the best tight end in football again.

Through five weeks, Kittle has caught 21 passes for 268 yards and four touchdowns. He has provided a passer rating of 129.2 when targeted.

His rapid recovery and return to form have been remarkable, especially considering that Kittle turned 33 earlier this month.

Plenty has gone wrong for the Seattle Seahawks during their 3-3 start to the season. Zach Charbonnet remains sidelined by last season's ACL tear, while rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price is injured, which has severely hindered the ground game.

More importantly, though, quarterback Sam Darnold has not looked anything like the Pro Bowl quarterback he was a year ago. He missed time after suffering a glute/hip injury early in Week 1 and has been exceedingly turnover-prone.

Backup Drew Lock, by comparison, was surprisingly effective while leading Seattle to a 2-0 start. While Darnold currently has a QB rating of just 77.4, Lock has an impressive 127.3 passer rating.

In his two appearances this season, Lock completed 72.9 percent of his passes for 422 yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions, and 13 rushing yards. His play was so surprisingly good that some analysts—including ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio —are now wondering whether Seattle should return to Lock on a more permanent basis.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels g ot his first career win in Week 5 and has been a recent surprise in 2026. However, the undrafted rookie out of Kansas was unexpectedly effective in Tampa's big road win in Dallas.

Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown, posting a 110.2 passer rating against the Cowboys, while adding 23 yards on the ground.

Still, Daniels' ascent to the starting role, albeit temporarily, ahead of Week 5 was surprising in its own right. After going undrafted in April, Daniels earned his opportunity with the Buccaneers by beating out Jake Browning for the backup QB job. He then got his first start in Week 4 after Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb.

An afterthought in April's draft, Daniels just became the first rookie quarterback to win in 2026.

Tennessee Titans fans haven't had a ton to get excited about during the team's 0-5 start to the season. However, they should be pleased with the rapid development of rookies Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr.

Tate leads the Titans' offense with 274 receiving yards, while Hill leads the defense with 47 tackles.

Tate's quick emergence probably isn't a major shocker, though, as Tennessee grabbed him with the fourth overall pick to fill their vacant No. 1 receiver role. Hill, who was taken late in the second round (60th overall), has been a much bigger surprise.

The 21-year-old has played 100 percent of the defensive snaps through four games and is currently on pace for a ridiculous 160 tackles as a rookie.

Washington Commanders: CB Amik Robertson

Cornerback Amik Robertson wasn't exactly an unknown commodity before joining the Washington Commanders this past offseason. He developed into a starter with the Las Vegas Raiders. He spent his last two seasons as a part-time starter and significant contributor in Detroit.

However, Robertson wasn't exactly viewed as a marquee addition. The 28-year-old signed a two-year, $15 million contract that he already appears to be outperforming.

Robertson has been one of the brightest spots on Washington's new-look defense. He has started all four games and has played 99 percent of the defensive snaps. He has already recorded 33 tackles and a league-high eight passes defended.

In coverage, Robertson has allowed an opposing passer rating of only 87.0 for the season.

articles.title: Justin Herbert, Madison Beer and the Chargers’ crisis: Why the quarterback’s love life isn’t the real problem
articles.summary: Justin Herbert has not won a game this season, and some fans have decided Madison Beer is the reason.
articles.body: Justin Herbert has not won a game this season, and some fans have decided Madison Beer is the reason. The Chargers fell to 0-5 with a 23-17 home loss to Denver on October 11, their worst start since 2003. Herbert threw for 121 yards and an interception, then took a sack as time ran out. The game film points elsewhere. Four rookies started on the offensive line, Herbert has been sacked 17 times in five games, and his head coach admits one bad call helped sink the afternoon. None of that has anything to do with his fiancée.Madison Beer is a distraction from what broke the offense?The theory is easy to mock. Justin Herbert and Madison Beer announced their engagement on July 28, right before training camp. Herbert said the proposal made him more nervous than his first NFL start, and in May he skipped part of the voluntary offseason program to support Beer on tour. At Seattle, a fan heckled him about her. “I truly blame Madison Beer for this loss,” one fan wrote on X after an earlier defeat. That kind of noise follows any high-profile couple. But nothing in the results suggests a quarterback who stopped working.The Denver game shows what actually happened.Los Angeles led 17-10 entering the fourth quarter, and its defense held Denver to 224 total yards and 1 of 12 on third down. Then Harbaugh called a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-one from his own 41, and it failed. “It was the wrong decision,” Harbaugh said afterward. He took full responsibility for the call. Herbert later threw an interception that set up a Denver field goal, and the game ended on another sack before he could get a Hail Mary off. His 14-of-24 line was ugly. The collapse belonged to more people than him.Protection and penalties keep burying the offenseDenver sacked Herbert five times, pushing his season total to 17. He came up limping when Nik Bonitto pulled him down by the left leg, the kind of hit the Chargers hoped to cut down when they brought in Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator. Herbert has played through thin lines before, but not like this. Injuries held out several linemen and most of the top receivers. Ladd McConkey, his most reliable target, missed the game with a foot injury. "It's tough," Herbert said.Discipline is another leak. The Chargers drew 16 penalties for 130 yards in Seattle. Herbert had only 816 passing yards and four touchdowns through four weeks, thin numbers for him. AP noted he spent the last two seasons fixing whatever ailed this offense. This year, the fix isn't working.Harbaugh has apologized, and his players are backing him. That helps the locker room, not the standings. What the Chargers need is healthy tackles, cleaner Sundays and a few early drives that end in points. Beer cannot supply any of that. articles.summary: Week 6 got off to a rather uninspired start in the world of fantasy. While Jaxon Smith-Njigba had a typical high-volume outing, the Denver Broncos won a 17-14 game against the Seattle Seahawks that was anything but a cascade of fantasy scoring.
articles.body:
Week 6 got off to a rather uninspired start in the world of fantasy. While Jaxon Smith-Njigba had a typical high-volume outing, the Denver Broncos won a 17-14 game against the Seattle Seahawks that was anything but a cascade of fantasy scoring.

Unfortunately, any managers looking to play catch-up over the rest of the weekend will have to deal with a flood of key injuries, along with another set of byes. The Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, and Minnesota Vikings are all off this week.

The good news is that a few viable fill-ins should still be available on the late-week waiver wire.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 6 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining point-per-reception (PPR) options, and highlight some sleepers who may still be available on the waiver wire.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is set to miss another game with his ankle injury, meaning Tyler Huntley will start for the second straight week. He's a viable sleeper, rostered in only two percent of leagues, against the Cleveland Browns this week.

While Jackson will be out, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) may make his return. Officially, he's questionable, but Williams was a full participant in practice on both Thursday and Friday. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers, meanwhile, are not ready to insert Baker Mayfield (thumb) back into the lineup.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Week 6 with a superficial blood clot.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins is probably the top target for Week 6, as he'll face a suspect Buffalo Bills defense at home. However, he's already rostered in 69 percent of fantasy leagues.

Jameis Winston is a solid Plan B at QB and is only rostered in 20 percent of leagues. He has delivered 20-plus fantasy points in back-to-back weeks and will face a middling New Orleans Saints defense on Sunday.

The Saints have surrendered an average of 17.1 fantasy points to opposing QBs in 2026.

Aaron Rodgers and Michael Penix Jr. are also reasonable sleepers to consider in Week 6.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Along with Hurts, the Eagles have ruled out running back Saquon Barkley. The list of RBs ruled out this week also includes Will Shipley, Kyle Monangai, Dylan Sampson, and AJ Dillon.

TreVeyon Henderson, Quinshon Judkins, Alvin Kamara, Tyjae Spears, Rico Dowdle, and Sean Tucker are listed as questionable.

New York Jets running back Breece Hall isn't quite ready to return from his quad injury, meaning Braelon Allen should start for the third straight week. Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, meanwhile, will miss a game for the first time after playing through ankle injuries in the early season.

Because of Love's ankle injury, Tyler Allgeier is a strong add for Week 6. He has only reached double-digit fantasy points once this season but should see a higher volume against the Los Angeles Rams.

The Rams, meanwhile, have been relatively average against opposing RBs in fantasy, surrendering an average of 17.4 points to opposing backfields in 2026. Allgeier is still only rostered in 44 percent of fantasy leagues.

Woody Marks figures to be another backup-turned-starter with David Montgomery set to miss time with a groin injury. While the Houston Texans will face a Jacksonville Jaguars team that has surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs, he should have a serviceable PPR floor. The bigger issue is that Marks was a popular waiver claim and is now rostered in 79 percent of leagues.

It's worth checking to see if Marks is still available. Kendre Miller, Mike Washington Jr., Kaelon Black, and far more realistic targets late in the week, albeit with lower floors as well.

While Hurts and Barkley have been ruled out, DeVonta Smith is set to make his return for Philadelphia. A.J. Brown is questionable but could also return for the New England Patriots. However, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, Tre' Harris, Rashee Rice, Skyy Moore, and Tank Dell are out.

D.J. Moore, Ja'Kobi Lane, Omar Cooper Jr., Chris Olave, DK Metcalf, and David Sills are listed as questionable.

Indianapolis Colts receiver Keenan Allen projects as a solid fill-in this week and a viable flex option for as long as he's healthy and Alec Pierce remains sidelined.

Allen delivered 15.3 fantasy points in Week 3, missed Week 4, and yielded a modest seven points in Week 5. However, he has a solid matchup against a Tennessee Titans defense that has surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points (tied) to opposing WRs this season.

Allen is rostered in only 40 percent of leagues.

With receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson both sidelined by injuries, rookie Germie Bernard should be a reasonable play for the Pittsburgh Steelers this week. He logged 14.4 fantasy points last week and is rostered in only 34 percent of fantasy leagues.

Keon Coleman, Kendrick Bourne, Tre Tucker, and Makai Lemon are other strong waiver options to consider this week.

The list of notable tight ends who are on this week's injury report is pretty much limited to Colts tight end Tyler Warren and Jets rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who are both questionable. However, Sam LaPorta and T.J. Hockenson are on bye.

Managers who need a fill-in at tight end this week should consider Pittsburgh's Pat Freiermuth. The Steelers' injuries at wide receiver should make him a go-to option in Week 6, and he's coming off a 21.5-point performance in Week 6.

Freiermuth will also face a Buccaneers defense that has surrendered an average of 12.7 fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season. He's rostered in 48 percent of leagues.

The list of sleeper tight ends who may still be available this week also includes Tyler Higbee, Brenton Strange, Chigoziem Okonkwo, and Oronde Gadsden II.

articles.body: Josh Allen has given the Buffalo Bills a strong start to the 2026 NFL season, and the betting market now places him ahead of the field in the race for the MVP award. Buffalo is 4-1 after five games, with Allen producing through the air and on the ground. DraftKings Sportsbook lists him at +240 to win his second career MVP, ahead of San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy at +300. The numbers put Allen in a strong position, but the bigger question is whether his individual form can help Buffalo make a deeper playoff run.Josh Allen's MVP odds reflect his impact on BuffaloJosh Allen's position at the top of the betting market is backed by a productive opening stretch. He has thrown for 1,249 yards, completed 65.9% of his passes and recorded seven touchdowns against four interceptions through five games. His passer rating stands at 99.6. Those numbers show a quarterback who has helped Buffalo win consistently, even if his passing totals alone do not tell the full story.His work as a runner is a major part of the case. Allen has rushed for 239 yards and scored eight touchdowns on the ground, the most rushing touchdowns in the league at this stage of the season, according to Heavy's report. That ability gives Buffalo another way to move the ball when passing lanes close or a play breaks down.It also makes Allen difficult to defend. Opponents cannot focus only on his receivers or expect him to remain in the pocket. He can extend a play with his arm, pick up yards himself or finish a drive near the goal line. That range of options helps explain why he has moved ahead of established names such as Patrick Mahomes, who is listed at +600, in the current MVP betting market.Still, +240 is a snapshot of how bookmakers view the race, not a guarantee of where it will finish. Thirteen regular-season weeks remain, leaving plenty of room for another quarterback to take the lead.Buffalo's playoff ambitions could shape Josh Allen's MVP caseThe more pressing issue for Allen is how Buffalo builds on its 4-1 start. The Bills lead the AFC East and sit fourth in the conference, giving them a solid early position. Yet the regular season will test whether they can maintain that pace against tougher opponents and carry their form into January.Allen's production gives Buffalo a reliable foundation, but his award chances will depend on more than his ability to score touchdowns. The team's results, his consistency and the performances of rival quarterbacks will all shape the race. His four interceptions also show that there is room to improve, even with his strong overall numbers.Buffalo's next test comes against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, October 18. The matchup offers another chance for Allen to strengthen his MVP case while helping the Bills protect their place near the top of the AFC.The distinction is important: Allen can put together an award-worthy season without the Bills winning the Super Bowl. But Buffalo's larger goal is to turn regular-season success into a deep postseason run. His MVP odds show how highly he is rated right now. articles.title: Haley Cavinder reveals the unexpected DM from Cowboys star Jake Ferguson that changed her love life forever: “Married life is great"
articles.summary: Haley Cavinder was not looking for a relationship when Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson first contacted her.
articles.body: Haley Cavinder was not looking for a relationship when Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson first contacted her. But one simple question about her golf game turned into a romance that led to their marriage in June. During an appearance on PEOPLE’s WAG World series, Cavinder revealed how Ferguson made the first move and why her initial impression of him has lasted. The 25-year-old, who has millions of followers across social media, also explained how her twin sister Hanna helped shape her view of the NFL star before their relationship became serious.Jake Ferguson started their relationship with a simple DM“He just DMed me and asked how my golf game was,” Haley told WAG World host Skyler Caruso on Friday, October 9.The opening message was casual, but their connection developed quickly. Haley had graduated from the University of Miami in 2023, placing her near Ferguson’s family in Florida. His mother had a home in Fort Myers Beach, while Haley’s grandparents lived in Naples. The two locations were about two hours apart, making it easier for the couple to spend time together.“When I first met Jake, I just graduated from the University of Miami,” she recalled.Neither person was necessarily searching for a serious relationship. Haley said she preferred to keep her expectations in check rather than become too invested too soon.“I don’t like to get high or too low when it comes to that stuff,” she said. “I wasn’t looking for anything, and I don’t know if Ferg was at that time either. But then we spent 10 days together straight, and he’s just a good, down-to-earth human being.”Those 10 days gave her a clearer picture of the person behind the Cowboys uniform. Dating a professional athlete can bring its own challenges, particularly when public attention becomes part of a relationship. Haley said Ferguson stood out because his personality away from football matched what she had hoped to find.“Right away I was just like, wow, outside of who he is on the field, dating athletes in this space and even probably dating us, we all come with a lot and being in the environment, you never know what you’re going to get,” she said. “I found a good one. My first impression is still who he is today.”She added, “He’s just really, really grounded. He makes me better in everything.”Hanna Cavinder’s approval came before the weddingFerguson also had to win over Haley’s twin sister. Hanna admitted she initially struggled to believe the Cowboys player was as genuine as he seemed.“I thought it was fake, really, because I thought that’s way too good to be true. There’s no way somebody’s going to continue that,” Hanna said. She wanted to see whether his behavior would last six months.For Haley, Hanna’s opinion carried considerable weight. The sisters share a close bond, and Haley wanted the person she was dating to earn the trust of the person who knew her best.“Hanna’s the most important human being in my life, and I think that she knows me best,” Haley said.Ferguson eventually passed that test. He proposed on a beach in April 2025, and the couple married on June 20, 2026, at Miami’s Biltmore Hotel in a beachfront ceremony.Haley said marriage has not dramatically changed their relationship. “Married life is great... I think that it’s just what we were doing. I think nothing’s changed. I still feel like we’re dating, but we’re married,” she said.She acknowledged that their bond now carries a deeper commitment. “I think that maybe it’s more serious, I would say. Serious meaning we’re family now. I have my family, but now we have our family... and my little puppy, Boozer.”For Haley, Ferguson’s appeal was never just his NFL career or public profile. articles.body: Brittany Mahomes had a brief response after Kylie Kelce publicly praised her work in women's sports, bringing attention to a role that extends well beyond her connection to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The Dallas Cowboys fell to No. 18 in the NFL power rankings after suffering a damaging loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The defeat exposed weaknesses on both sides of the ball and raised fresh doubts about whether the team has the consistency needed to compete with the league's top contenders.

The loss was particularly concerning because Tampa Bay entered the matchup without a victory. Instead of taking advantage of the opportunity, Dallas struggled to contain the opposing offense and failed to produce the scoring output usually needed to secure wins. The Cowboys managed just 16 points, a disappointing total for a team that often relies on offensive firepower to overcome its defensive shortcomings.

Running back Bucky Irving played a major role in Tampa Bay's success by finding room against a defense that struggled to slow him down. Quarterback Jalon Daniels also delivered a credible performance while filling in for Baker Mayfield, helping the visitors remain productive despite the change under center. Their contributions highlighted how effectively Tampa Bay exploited its opportunities against a Dallas team expected to control the matchup.

The offensive struggles were just as damaging. Dallas has often depended on its ability to score at a high rate, but that approach becomes difficult to sustain when drives stall and points are limited. Without enough production from the offense, the defense faces greater pressure to make stops and prevent opponents from building an advantage. The latest defeat showed how vulnerable the team can become when its usual formula fails.

Dallas Cowboys Drop in Latest NFL Power Rankings After Losing to Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Dak Prescott-led team fell in the latest power rankings after losing to the Buccaneers. This is detailed in an analysis by Nick Shook for the league's official website.

The Cowboys suffered a disastrous loss on Thursday night, falling to a previously winless Buccaneers team that had every reason to lay down in Arlington. Instead, Bucky Irving ran through Dallas' defense, Jalon Daniels produced a creditable performance in place of Baker Mayfield, and the Cowboys' typically-explosive offense mustered just 16 points. We know Dallas only has one path to victory — light up the scoreboard — and when that doesn't work, it exposes the flaws in this club. It's only one loss, but it eliminated much of my confidence in this team being a real contender.

The drop to No. 18 reflects the growing concern surrounding the Cowboys' overall reliability. One loss does not define an entire season, but losing to a previously winless opponent makes it harder to dismiss the performance as an isolated setback. The team must address its defensive problems while finding ways to produce more consistent results on offense.

Dallas now faces pressure to respond with a stronger all-around performance in its next game. Improved tackling, better defensive discipline and more efficient scoring will be essential if the team hopes to restore confidence in its playoff prospects. Until those improvements appear consistently, questions about the Cowboys ' status as legitimate contenders are likely to persist.

articles.title: No running game. A trade for a top receiver. How the Texans' offensive approach has shifted
articles.summary: Houston built its 2026 roster to run the ball, but C.J. Stroud and the passing game have carried the Texans as they add Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.body:
LONDON - Before the 2026 season began, the Houston Texans made moves to improve their running game.

Drafting Keylan Rutledge in the first round? Run game.

Signing Foster Moreau, Wyatt Teller and Braden Smith in free agency? Run game.

The Texans wanted to be a team that could run the ball well, take care of the football and let its defense do what it does best - a formula they thought would help them win games.

But the opposite has happened through the first five games of 2026.

The Texans have slowly morphed into a pass-first team by necessity, led by their fourth-year quarterback, C.J. Stroud . And with their latest move - acquiring wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade - the Texans appear to be settling into that newfound identity.

When the Texans traded for Harrison, their receivers were playing their best football, as was their quarterback, who is off to the best five-game stretch of his career.

Harrison's arrival gives Houston the ability to take its passing game to another level and lean heavily into one area of the team that has remained consistent: passing the football.

The Texans rank sixth in the NFL in passing offense.

That doesn't mean the Texans will rely exclusively on the pass and abandon the run. Offensive coordinator Nick Caley still wants to maintain balance in his offense.

But it does mean the Texans know their strengths and how to use them to address their biggest weaknesses.

The Texans have struggled to run the ball for most of the season. They are averaging 3.4 yards per carry, 30th in the NFL.

They have even struggled to gain a yard in fourth-and-inches situations, a task that could become more difficult Sunday against the league's stingiest run defense. The Jaguars allow just 64 rushing yards per game.

But leaning into the passing game, especially on first downs, could open things up in the running game.

Running back Woody Marks rushed for 62 yards on 15 carries - the most rushing yards by a Texans running back this season. He also had a 24-yard touchdown run nullified by a holding penalty.

"You can't sit there and be completely one-dimensional," Caley said. "I think you have to have some level of balance, and I think that goes back to finding the opportune times to be able to consistently, whether it's throwing the ball, whether it's sticking to the runs, whether it's starting with a run-first mentality or a throw-first mentality."

The Texans passed on 16 of their 26 first-down attempts. That led to lighter boxes from the Titans on early downs and more efficient runs by the Texans. Marks had two runs of 12 yards or more on first down in last week's win.

It was also the first time since Week 1 that Marks or David Montgomery averaged more than 4 yards per carry in a game.

Montgomery is out with a groin injury Sunday, so Marks will start. The Texans will also call up running back Jawhar Jordan from the practice squad.

"He's explosive," Caley said of Marks. "He can put his foot in the ground and be a slash runner. He's got good play speed. He does a good job in pass protection as well, not to mention the run game stuff. And in the pass game, he can catch the ball and make people miss."

Harrison's addition also gives the Texans another talented receiver.

Stroud is used to playing with a bevy of top receivers and distributing the ball. That helped make him one of the best quarterbacks in the country.

At Ohio State, he played with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave, Garrett Wilson and Emeka Egbuka, all of whom have gone on to become star NFL receivers. Harrison was a freshman on that team.

Harrison likely won't contribute much immediately. He still has to learn the playbook, and Caley still has to figure out how to use him.

But the Texans have a few plays for him that they hope to use Sunday against the Jaguars. They see his addition as an enhancement.

"All of our guys are still going out making plays that we expect them to make - (Xavier Hutchinson), Nico (Collins), (Jaylin Noel), (Kayshon Boutte), all those guys that welcomed Marvin in really well. They welcomed him with open arms, and Marvin is fitting in just fine," coach DeMeco Ryans said. "We'll try to get him as much action as he can handle on Sundays, so I'm just excited about the group. Anytime you can add depth to that wide receiver room, it makes it more challenging on defenses, and that's what we want to do."

articles.title: Peter King says it’s ‘ridiculous’ Mike Shanahan isn’t in Hall of Fame
articles.summary: "When John Elway tells me that Mike Shanahan, far and away was the major reason we won Super Bowl 32, [that] says something to me," Peter King said.
articles.body:
When it comes to the Pro Football Hall of Fame and their short list of coach candidates ripe for enshrinement, there is one in the mind of NFL analyst Peter King that has continued to be overlooked: former Denver Broncos coach Mike Shanahan.

Shanahan was straight from the San Francisco 49ers, right out of Hall of Fame coach Bill Walsh's West Coast offense, one of the most potent offensive schemes in NFL history. Shanahan won a Super Bowl as an offensive coordinator for the 49ers before coming to Denver and turning the fortune of the Broncos in a championship trajectory. In his third and fourth seasons as Broncos coach, Shanahan helped Denver win their first titles in team history, eventually becoming the most successful coach in franchise history (138-86), which is good for 20th in all-time victories .

In a recent appearance on "The Dan Patrick Show," King fiercely advocated for Shanahan's recognition.

"I think it's ridiculous," King said of Shanahan not being in the Hall of Fame.

Patrick agreed with King, asking, "How do you not put the guy who might have the best coaching tree, or one of the best coaching trees and success in the history of the sport?"

"When I was a voter (for the Pro Football Hall of Fame), I staunchly advocated for Shanahan," King said.

King went on to tell a story about Super Bowl XXXII, where Shanahan pinpointed Green Bay Packers defensive back Leroy Butler as the most pivotal player of the game. In order to take away Butler's influence, Shanahan put Hall of Fame tight end Shannon Sharpe out wide in the formation, taking Butler almost completely out of the game.

"When John Elway tells me that Mike Shanahan, far and away was the major reason we won that Super Bowl, says something to me," King said.

In the past year, King again pleaded for Shanahan's inclusion in the Hall of Fame. King is not alone in his opinion, as Hall of Famer Champ Bailey came out earlier this year in Shanahan's defense for enshrinement.

Shanahan's coaching tree is one of the most successful in the NFL today. You can see his fingerprints throughout the league, from Sean McVay's Los Angeles Rams to Liam Coen's Jacksonville Jaguars, and of course, Kyle Shanahan's San Francisco 49ers.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame recently overhauled its voting guidelines after the snub of Bill Belichick from the Class of 2026, which could slow down Shanahan's bid to get his bronze bust displayed in Canton.

He certainly has his fair share of defenders and advocates to help get him there, and Shanahan figures to eventually reach the Hall of Fame.
